fix.summary:
All thirteen findings are decided and the design is corrected; every one is "fixed", none is left for a builder or for the user. The lint is clean and the ledger shows no open D33 entry.

The major one, D33R-C-1, is settled in one place, T-REMOTE in `/Users/jmagady/dev2/vsdd-factory/rewrite/spec/tables/sync-checks.toml`:
- **Push:** `git push <remote> <source>:refs/heads/<branch>`, where the source is the branch or the id of a commit built on the remote's head.
- **Fetch:** `git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`, never into a ref under `refs/heads/`.
- **Nothing else:** no `git pull` and no fetch without a refspec, so no fetch can move the mounted state branch, a person's target branch or a story branch.

I ran every git-dependent claim in scratch repositories (a bare remote, two clones with remotes named `shared` and `upstream`, a third plain copy) on git 2.34.1 in an Ubuntu 22.04 container and on 2.50.1 on macOS. Only what I saw went into `team-git-facts.md`: facts 6 and 9 are corrected and facts 15 to 18 are new. The full sync, the two-clone claim and the hand-off were walked command by command three times on each version, with either clone winning the claim; every command exited as designed and no integration branch moved, local or remote.

Three things the tests showed went past what the findings proposed:
- **A fetch into the state branch is worse on the floor git than reported.** Run from the main checkout on 2.34.1 it exits 0 and silently moves the branch under the mount; on 2.50.1 it exits 128.
- **A plain push undoes a rewind silently.** If the state branch is moved back to a bare ancestor between a clone's fetch and its push, the push is a fast-forward, exits 0 and restores the removed commit, so no judging ever runs. Every state push now names the head it was built on (`--force-with-lease=<ref>:<head>`); that was refused with the remote untouched in the same test, gave exactly one winner in 20 rounds of 20, and was accepted by a remote that forbids non-fast-forward updates.
- **The old "somebody replaced the branch" test misfires on the holder's own push.** After a forced story push whose answer was lost, the remote head is the holder's own head but does not contain `delivery.pushed`. Separately, merging a teammate's commit into a rebase the remote never took leaves each of the holder's commits in history twice.

Two things to know about the ledger:
- **D33-13 was closed as fixed by the survey unit while I worked.** The built `target_head` fetches into the remote-tracking ref, which is right, but without the leading `+` and without asserting that the local branch stayed put. I recorded that remainder as a new entry, D33-33, for S3 and G4a; it is pr-mode only, which the slice does not run.
- **Two more builder entries are new:** D33-31 (one job-layer field so a finished sync is never served to a later call, for M1) and D33-32 (the survey's batch function and a readable close reserve, for M2 and B4a).

The test scripts are in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jmagady-dev2-vsdd-factory/f468fc16-2190-4e04-8bbb-50654bb31906/scratchpad/gt/` (`common.sh`, `t1_fetch.sh`, `t2_rename.sh`, `t2b_rename.sh`, `t3_push.sh`, `t4_walks.sh`, `t5_story.sh`). I removed the scratch container afterwards.
decisions_made: Every fetch is `git fetch <remote> +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<remote>/<b>` and every push is `git push <remote> <source>:refs/heads/<b>`; the tool runs no `git pull` and no fetch without a refspec (T-REMOTE).
What a clone last saw on the remote is `sync.remote_head` (state) or `delivery.pushed` (story), never the remote-tracking ref, which any fetch moves.

Every push of the state branch carries `--force-with-lease` naming the head it was built on, and the tool refuses to push a commit that does not contain that head; a plain push silently restores commits after a rewind to an ancestor.
`--force` is passed to no push; only two pushes carry a lease (state branch, and the story branch after the tool's own rebase), each naming the head it expects.
After a failed state push the tool lists, fetches and runs T-HISTORY first; `rewritten` and `missing` go to every caller, and a lost race requires the new head to contain the base.
After a lost race T-PUBLISH and T-MINT repeat from their opening sync, so arrivals pass T-INCOMING and T-HOLD before anything is built again.
`sync.remote_head` is written only when T-HISTORY passes a fetched head or when a push of this clone is accepted.
Changed-path lists are read by one M1 function with `git diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-status -z`, stated once as a head rule of table:team-checks.
A wait for `local/sync.lock` counts against the caller's budget (60 s in a foreground command, ten minutes in a job) and ends in `busy` with nothing changed.
A command that takes a claim, mints an id or opens a cycle holds `local/sync.lock` for its whole act; this is what lets a full sync safely remove an `open` claim with no cycle record.
'Begun' is defined once in T-RELEASE, from the local branch or the closure's `delivery.pushed`, with no network call.
Auto-removal of claims keys on the claim's `run`: `vsdd claim take`, T-SWITCH and a T-SOLO join write an empty `run`, and no sync removes such a claim until a run enters it or it is released.
The sync result and the clone record gain `settled`, and a mint command run again after a lost answer returns the id already minted instead of minting a second.
A sync job's worker marks its own result collected, so a finished sync is never served to a later call (ledger D33-31, package M1).
The sync started by the `decisions` rule is its own job keyed `settle:<decision id>`, which names the one record its flush commits; it is always partial.
A clone that joins a team through T-SOLO runs the preflight and claims its in-flight stories as T-SWITCH does.
The head of table:team-checks is the one list of checks that act with team use off; it now includes T-DELIVERY in pr mode, T-REMOTE's ref rule and T-ORDER.
T-ORDER is independent of `team.enabled`, so records written before team use is turned on already carry their links.
With team use off `delivery.merged_by` holds no clone, and the person only where git has one to give.

A wave run claims batch N = min(stories_per_wave_run, agent fit with step_attempts counted as spent) and the survey returns N as `stories_per_run`; over-claiming by other scripts that spend agents first is stated as unmeasured (ledger D33-32).
Story-branch pushes are judged by fetch and comparison, not exit status; the tool rebases only from `delivery.pushed` and puts the branch back only when a fetch shows the push was not taken.
A story branch counts as replaced by somebody only when the remote head contains neither `delivery.pushed` nor this clone's head.
A rebase the remote never took is put back at `delivery.pushed` before a teammate's commit is merged in, guarded by `git cherry`; otherwise the unit is blocked as a conflict.
A holder with no local story branch creates it at the commit id of `delivery.pushed`; `git ls-remote --exit-code` (exit 2 = absent) says whether a story branch is on the remote.
Rejected from D33R-C-9: dropping arrived commits by patch id. Rejected from D33R-C-4: measuring 'begun' on the remote branch over the network and keying on `taken_from`.
D33-13 was closed by the survey unit during this work, so the missing `+` and two test assertions in the built `target_head` are a new entry, D33-33, for S3 and G4a.

I ran the git facts the corrections rest on myself, with scratch repositories, on git 2.50.1 (macOS) and git 2.34.1 (Ubuntu 22.04 container).
- Fact 15: a fetch into refs/heads/state exits 128 inside the mount on both versions. From the main checkout it exits 128 on 2.50.1 but 0 on 2.34.1, where it moves the branch under the mount and leaves a staged change. A fetch into a target branch that is not checked out exits 0 and moves it. A `+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>` fetch exits 0 and moves only the remote-tracking ref.
- Fact 9: after a rewind the fetch without `+` exits 1 with non-fast-forward, and with `+` it exits 0. `ls-remote --exit-code` gives 2 for an absent branch and 128 for a bad remote; a fetch gives 128 for both.
- Fact 16: after a rewind to an ancestor, a plain push exits 0 and restores the removed commit. The lease push exits 1 with stale info and leaves the remote alone. With the remote at H the lease push is accepted; with the remote moved forward it is refused stale. Under receive.denyNonFastForwards and receive.denyDeletes the lease push is accepted, and a lease push of a commit that does not contain the remote head is refused.
- Fact 6: `git diff --name-status` and `git show --name-status` list a release plus a take as R086. `git diff-tree -r`, with or without `--no-renames` and whatever diff.renames is set to, lists D and A, and `-M` joins them. My three-line claims still showed R058, which supports the fact's own conclusion that the rename follows how alike the files are; the design rests on `--no-renames` alone.
- Facts 13 and 17: the listing gives only the teammate's commit. A merge into the rebased branch leaves the holder's commit twice. Putting the branch back and fast-forwarding gives it once. `git cherry` marks the rebased copies `-` and a commit made after the rebase `+`.

fix.summary:
All four findings are fixed in the design, and the lint, coverage, brief generation and ledger build are clean. I also recorded one new open gap for package M4, `D33-34`, which I did not settle.

- **D33R-C-3 (arrivals after a lost race).** `sync.remote_head` now means the last remote head whose arrivals the clone checked and took into its mount. A fetch made only to judge a push no longer moves it, so the repeated sync checks every commit between the push's base and the new head. Confirmed on git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1: the commits that beat a push reached the mount unchecked by the fast-forward alone, and are caught when the listing starts from the base.
- **D33R-C-7 (a second list of what acts with team use off).** `topics/team-sync.md` now links to the head rule of `tables/team-checks.toml`. The same claim sat in two more places, `commands/sync.md` and T-SOLO, and both are corrected.
- **d33-fix-2-C1-1 (a second request given the first one's id).** T-MINT now returns a settled id only to a command whose request digest matches the one stored with the lost answer. A different request mints a new id.
- **d33-fix-2-C1-2 (a network listing in local mode).** T-BRANCH asks the remote about a story branch only when the closure records `delivery.pushed` or the local branch has an upstream. Both are read without the network, so local mode makes no call.

Two things the git runs showed went past what the findings asked:

- **`git ls-remote` matches at the end of a name.** With only `keep/refs/heads/story/S-6` on the remote, a listing of `refs/heads/story/S-6` exits 0. Every listing is now read by exact ref name, for the state branch as well.
- **The step-3 shortcut of `vsdd sync` skipped more than the fetch.** It also skipped settling commits with a lost answer and removing stale claims, so on a quiet remote a minting command would stay refused. The shortcut now requires those to be empty too.

The new entry `D33-34`: the survey's listing and fetch for each held story have a per-call time limit but no shared budget, and no row says what the survey does with a story whose branch could not be read. T-FRESH's claim that the survey stays inside two minutes does not account for them. It is in the ledger as open, triaged to M4, with a proposed resolution.

`tables/work-claim-checks.toml` is now 43 bytes under the 16 KB limit, so any further addition there must remove text. I edited `schemas/clone.schema.json`, which the task did not name but which D33 registered. The experiment script is `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jmagady-dev2-vsdd-factory/f468fc16-2190-4e04-8bbb-50654bb31906/scratchpad/gitfacts/facts.sh`; it ran three rounds on each git version with no failures.
decisions_made: sync.remote_head means the last remote head whose arrivals the clone checked and took into its mount; it is written only after the mount holds the commit, at step 4 of the sync (the fetched head) and at an accepted push (the pushed commit, never the remote's head).
A fetch made to judge a push writes nothing to the mount or the clone record; T-HISTORY reads sync.remote_head and never writes it.

The step-3 shortcut of vsdd sync needs four conditions: listed head equals sync.remote_head, the mount's head equals it too, sync.unknown is empty, and in a full sync no claim is due for removal by T-RELEASE. The last two go past the finding, because the shortcut also skipped step 4's own-clone work.
A lost race still repeats from the listing and does not reuse the judging fetch: two more network calls per lost race, kept for a rule that is plainly correct.
The request digest for a minted id is kept in the clone record, which stays on the machine, and not as a commit trailer or by comparing files; sync.unknown entries become objects {commit, request}.
The digest covers the kind of id and every caller-given value of the new file, and nothing the tool adds; one function of package M3 computes it for all six minting commands.
A minting command removes a settled entry whose request equals its own whether or not the remote took the commit; a command with another request leaves the entries for vsdd status and the briefing.
Not measured, and stated in T-MINT: a request reworded after a lost answer is minted again.

T-BRANCH asks the remote about a story branch only when the closure records delivery.pushed or the local branch has an upstream. A first push whose answer and judging fetch were both lost is caught at the next push, not by a survey listing.

Every listing of one branch is read by its exact ref name, through one function of package M1, because git ls-remote matches at the end of a name; this applies to the state branch (T-HISTORY) as well as story branches.
T-BRANCH returns the unit blocked when the story branch is gone from the remote and the clone does not hold the commit delivery.pushed names.
When each hand-commit check acts is stated only in its own runs cell; T-NOTICE's condition (the target branch has an upstream) is unchanged.
T-SOLO and commands/sync.md no longer claim to be the only change with team use off; the head of tables/team-checks.toml is the one list.

The survey's unbounded network time for held story branches is recorded as open ledger entry D33-34 for M4 and not settled here, because settling it means deciding what the survey returns for a story it could not read.

Findings. D33R-C-3 is confirmed fixed. T-HISTORY now reads sync.remote_head and never writes it. The field is written only at step 4 after the fast-forward, or at an accepted push to the pushed commit, and a judging fetch writes nothing. So after a lost race the repeated sync, and T-PUBLISH's and T-MINT's repeated opening sync, list what arrived from the push's base. The step-3 shortcut in commands/sync.md now also requires the mount's head to equal sync.remote_head, an empty sync.unknown, and no claim due for removal by T-RELEASE. Proof scenario 2 covers both cases. D33R-C-7 is confirmed fixed. The last section of topics/team-sync.md, commands/sync.md and T-SOLO now point to the head rule of table:team-checks and keep no list of their own, and team-use.md and config/team.md agree. d33-fix-2-C1-1 is confirmed fixed. The request digest is defined once, in records/clone.md, and sync.unknown entries are objects {commit, request} in the schema. T-MINT returns an id only for an equal request, the reworded-request residue is stated in its unmeasured cell, scenario 30 is extended, and M3 delivers the digest function. d33-fix-2-C1-2 is confirmed fixed for T-BRANCH. Its runs cell is the one condition and is read without the network, and the head rule, team-delivery.md, survey.md and story-deliver.md refer to it. The exact-name listing rule matches fact 19, the fifth blocked case matches fact 21, and scenarios 23 and 38 assert that no listing is made. D33-34 is triaged to M4 and appears in rewrite/findings/by-package/M4.md. Nothing on the slice path changed: the passages touched in survey.md and story-deliver.md are their D33 sections.

The design choices work as specified and can be enforced, with four new minor problems listed under still_open. First, T-NEVER's runs cell lost the local test the old head rule gave it. Second, survey.md, gate-wave.md and gate-release.md still repeat T-NOTICE's condition, though the rule now says it is stated nowhere else. Third, "written in two places only" leaves no value for sync.remote_head when a clone record is made (vsdd init join, T-SWITCH, T-SOLO's join, remade), and the writers are restated in record:clone, the schema and T-PUSH. still_open.problem: New, from the correction of d33-fix-2-C1-2. The head rule no longer gives the hand-commit checks the local condition 'the branch they read has an upstream'; it says each condition is stated only in the check's own runs cell. T-NEVER's runs cell reads 'At every git command the tool runs on a branch that is on the remote', which is a property of the remote, and it gives no local test. A builder following it would list the remote before a rebase or squash in local mode, which config/team.md ('Off') and proof scenario 23 forbid. Where the remote cannot be listed, 'cannot measure is a failure' would refuse the delivery.
still_open.proposed_fix: State T-NEVER's runs cell as a test read without the network: a story branch for which T-BRANCH's runs cell has the remote asked (delivery.pushed recorded, or an upstream), and a target branch with an upstream. still_open.problem: New, from the correction of D33R-C-3. T-HISTORY says sync.remote_head is 'written in two places only': step 4 and an accepted push. Neither covers the moment a clone record is made. vsdd init writes the record on joining (T-JOIN), and the schema requires the field. T-SWITCH and T-SOLO's join make the record inside a sync whose T-HISTORY and T-INCOMING read the field before step 4 writes it, and a remade record has lost it. No file says what the field starts as, what the rewritten test compares, or what T-INCOMING checks on a first team sync. still_open.proposed_fix: In T-HISTORY, name the starting value of a new record: the merge base of the mount's head and the fetched head, written once the mount holds it. For T-JOIN that is the mounted head. Keep T-HISTORY as the one statement of when the field is written. Cut record:clone and the schema to a one-line meaning with a link, and have T-PUSH link to T-HISTORY instead of restating it. Add to proof scenario 17 a failing record on the remote when B joins, which B's sync reports through T-INCOMING.

still_open.problem: New. T-BRANCH's runs cell now has the survey look for a story branch only where delivery.pushed is recorded or the branch has an upstream. After a first push whose answer was lost and whose judging fetch failed, the branch has neither, because git sets the upstream of push -u only on a reported success. The same row's last paragraph still says that then 'the next survey measures', which the runs cell rules out. The adopted design choice says the next push catches it, but no file says so.
still_open.proposed_fix: Reword T-BRANCH's last sentence: the next survey measures where the runs cell has it look, and a first push whose answer and fetch were both lost is measured at the branch's next push, which is judged as every push is. Add that case to proof scenario 44. Alternatively, have the tool write the upstream configuration before the first push, and correct T-REMOTE's first-push sentence to match.
